Westfield Utilities will replace 6.2 miles of cast iron water mains this year, the largest single-year replacement in the utility's history.

The pipes being replaced were laid between 1921 and 1948, and they account for about 70 percent of the main breaks the utility repaired last year.

Crews logged 143 main breaks in 2025, up from 98 in 2022, and each break cost an average of $11,400 to repair, not counting lost water.

The $19.5 million program is paid for by a state revolving loan at 1.1 percent interest and a 4 percent increase in the base water rate that took effect in July.

Work will move street by street from April through November, and residents will get a door hanger at least 72 hours before their water is shut off for a tie-in.

The utility expects the new ductile iron mains to last at least 80 years and to cut breaks on the replaced streets by more than 90 percent.
